text:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep on TP 8-gpu backward path and saw a big tail latency increase when seq_len > 8k and microbatch=1. traces point to a bunch of tiny all-reduces (3-20KB) dominating wall time. attaching summary below.

alex: perf counters (summary):
- compute util steady ~78%
- allreduce stall time increased from 4% -> 32%
- avg allreduce msg size: 12KB
- burst count: ~1200 ops/sec during backward

alex: hypothesis: NCCL ring suffers on many tiny messages due to per-op overhead; tree algo or aggregation could help.

maya: ugh yeah this matches what I saw on the layernorm shards — tiny grads from elementwise ops.

maya: did you try NCCL_TREE? I remember tree wins for <64KB in our older tests.

alex: tested ring vs tree on dev box (8xV100) — numbers:
```
ring: median allreduce 1.9ms, p95 6.4ms
tree: median 1.2ms, p95 2.8ms
```
but tree increases overall CPU work and we saw a 3% extra memcpy overhead.

sandeep: interesting. are these ops coming from kv-cache invalidation / chunking? or from TP shard grads?

alex: mostly TP shard grads + some small KV cache spill merges when context is large. microbatching=1 makes it worse.

julie: two quick levers: (1) aggregate contiguous tiny tensors before allreduce (we tried nvidia gatherv-style accumulate); (2) policy switch to TREE for messages < 64KB. both are non-invasive.

sandeep: aggregation patch is small — collect tensors until size >= X or count >= N, then allreduce. risk: increased latency tail for critical tensors if we wait. we should expose a deadline to flush.

alex: agreed. i'm prototyping aggregation with a flush-deadline of 250us. rough pseudo:
```
queue.push(tensor);
if (queue.total_bytes >= 65536 || queue.count >= 16 || now - queue.first_ts > 250us) flush();
```

alex: also tried switching NCCL algo heuristically: if msg_size < 64KB -> TREE else RING. improved p95 by ~40% in our microbatch microbench.

maya: can you share the microbench? i'll run on AMD nodes.

alex: pushing gist in a sec. basic harness: 8-gpu TP model, backward-only synthetic grads, measure allreduce latency histogram.

ci-bot: perf-run 1765009901 completed — results uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/tp/micromsg/1765009901/*. baseline vs agg+tree.

julie: note: on A100 with NVLINK, tree wins less dramatically; still ~15% p95 improvement. on slower interconnect (rdma over eth) tree is a clear win.

sandeep: any regression risks? switching algorithm at runtime sounds safe. aggregation small risk: memory spike if many small tensors queued. we should cap queue bytes to e.g., 1MB.

alex: good call — will cap at 1MB and add telemetry: queued_bytes, flush_count, wait_time distribution.

maya: also check kvcache eviction patterns — if kvcache chunking merges produce aligned larger tensors we might get less tiny ops. maybe tweak chunk size.

alex: yeah, kv chunking at 256B -> 1KB is the offender. bumping to 4KB reduces op count by ~3x but increases memory footprint ~5%. tradeoff depends on workload.

julie: propose rollout plan: 1) enable aggregation on canary for TP workloads, 2) add NCCL algo heuristic, 3) expose kv chunk size config, 4) monitor CPU memcpy and memory.

alex: I'll open a canary PR with feature gate and telemetry. assigning reviewers @maya, @sandeep.

maya: ack — will run on AMD and report.

sandeep: ack — will review agg patch and sanity-check memory.

julie: I'll add a dashboard tile for queued_bytes and allreduce p95.

alex: thanks team. goal: cut allreduce-driven tail by >30% without impacting mean latency. :crossed_fingers:

ci-bot: note: linked perf artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/tp/micromsg/1765009901/ (baseline), s3://redwood-perf/tp/micromsg/1765009975/ (agg+tree).
